notes: Impeachment-tribunal sitting: short exchanges, so the page carries ten printed labels. The chair is labelled without a parenthetical surname throughout. Two article numbers in Baglini's speech print as unmapped glyphs — the font has no Unicode mapping for the ordinal sign, so the text reads 'artículos 1(cid:47) y 2(cid:47)'. This page is the reason the parser keeps such blocks rather than dropping them: the surrounding words are real. Parenthesized stenographer notes are recorded as events, per the convention settled in July 2026: nobody utters the word, so the note is the stenographer recording what the chamber did, not speech. CORRECTED 21 September 2026: this annotation listed '(Lee:)' as an event, following the convention of July 2026 that every parenthesised note is one. It also gave '(Lee:)' as the first words of the secretary's turn, so the same printed words were counted twice. The brief of September 2026 (rule 3) makes a '(Lee:)' printed right after the secretary's label his turn, not an event, which is also how the HTML half of the corpus has always filed it. A blind re-reading from the page image, by an annotator not shown this file, agreed with this one on all ten turns in order and differed only here; it is kept at reference/gold/rereadings/gold_2003-08-20_p3.RE.json.
